title: Grateful Dead Live at Gym, S.U.N.Y. (early) on 1970-10-31
lineage: 1st transfer: Gordon Healy's Reel > TEAC A 2300SD > Jimmy Warburton's Reel (1st gen) - transferred by Jimmy Warburton 2nd transfer: 1st Gen Reel > Technics RS-1506 > Tascam DA-3000 (DSF 1-bit/5.6 MHz)> dBpoweramp > wav 24/96 - transferred by Matt Smith Lineage: Wav 24/96 > Adobe Audition 3 > iZotope RX8 Advanced > CD Wave > flac24
source: SBD >  WUSB-FM 90.1 Master Reel (1/2 track 10” 7.5 ips) > Gordon Healy's Reel

ai_review.summary: A decent Halloween early‑set capture – acoustic opener and some hard‑rocking numbers shine, but the audience tape is only as clear as a 1970 college gym recording can be.
ai_review.review: The recording preserves an unusual early‑set for Halloween with "Till the Morning Comes" opening the show and high‑energy cuts like "Hard to Handle", "China > Rider" and "Viola > Cumberland".  Sound quality is limited by the venue mic and shows occasional dropouts and splicing, yet it is probably the best version that exists of this 1970 NY college gym performance.

ai_rating.rationale: One reviewer rates it highly for its musical moments while another gives a zero rating, and the recording suffers from venue‑mic limitations and dropouts; overall the show is interesting but the audio is only average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Gym‑room audience mic gives a lo‑fi, slightly muddy sound; occasional dropouts and splicing noted, but overall clarity is as good as can be expected for the source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early Halloween set starts acoustic and then ramps into louder rockers, giving a varied but cohesive flow.
